summary: Preinstall hook downloads Bun runtime and executes obfuscated 727 KB bundled payload
details: @servicetitan/cp-api@1.115.7 advertises itself as a small axios-instance wrapper (dist/index.js), but its package.json declares scripts.preinstall = "node setup.mjs". setup.mjs downloads the Bun runtime from https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases at install time, chmods it executable in a temp directory, and invokes it against math_init.js — a sibling 727 KB file shipped in the tarball. math_init.js is a single-line heavily obfuscated program: a large numeric/string table (n7gIxM), a rotate/shuffle routine (WV8StW), and a character-code decoder (hc1jfK9) that reconstructs identifiers, strings, and any network destinations at runtime; no plaintext URLs are present in source. Fetching a second language runtime purely to run an obfuscated bundle whose behavior cannot be inspected statically has no relation to the declared axios-wrapper purpose. The preinstall hook fires automatically on npm install, so any consumer of this version executes the obfuscated payload under the installer's account before their build or test scripts run. This matches the alternate-runtime-dropper pattern used to bypass Node-focused scanners: the runtime install is from an official source (bun.sh/oven-sh) but the code then executed under that runtime is a shipped obfuscated blob that has no legitimate role in an axios wrapper.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
